winner.text: Use a pairwise within-user ranking loss instead of pointwise binary cross-entropy while retaining the parent architecture and features.
winner.rationale: The official objective is entirely ranking-based, with GAUC 0.6694 and nDCG@5 0.5367, but the parent is trained with pointwise BCE. A pairwise objective directly trains positive-over-negative ordering and is especially relevant when classification improvements do not translate to top-k ranking.
winner.exact_ablation: Replace only pointwise BCE optimization with a within-user pairwise logistic loss formed from positive-negative impression pairs; keep the same five features, additive scorer, optimizer settings, batch budget, checkpoint rule, and validation evaluator unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely increase approximately +0.002 to +0.006 because the loss directly targets positive-negative ordering within users.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Likely increase approximately +0.001 to +0.005, though it may trade off against GAUC if pair sampling underrepresents the few items that belong in the top five.

selection_rationale: Select the within-user pairwise ranking loss. It is ranked first by the Consultant, directly aligns training with the GAUC and nDCG@5 objectives, preserves the validated parent features and architecture, has the highest expected primary gain among the reliable candidates (+0.003), confidence 5, low leakage risk, and only medium runtime risk. This offers a more reliable improvement than higher-novelty architecture changes.
